messages.author: b28a3b94cb6f8a9f
messages.subject: Using a background image (continued)
parts:
Hi all,

Following this post, I can plot an image as background :)
http://groups.google.com/group/ggplot2/browse_thread/thread/beff7d92f05dc741

Currently, I set xlim and ylim to the size of the picture, and width
and height to 1npc. However, this does not allow to zoom on certain
parts of the plot. I am wondering whether there is a way to write an
enhanced background function that would
- display the pixmap following the x and y scales if they are
specified,
- set the scales to the pixmap size if they are not specified.

As I am not very familiar with the engine behind ggplot2, I would
appreciate any comment on whether this is doable or not? If yes, how
would you access the x and y limits (as it looks like they are
computed on display time)?

Thank you in advance for your help,

Thomas

parts:
Hi,

Last time I thought about this I convinced myself that one should
write a geom_raster for ggplot2. Unfortunately, I haven't found the
time / understanding required to write one. My lame attempt at
borrowing code from lattice::panel.levelplot.raster resulted in this,


library(ggplot2)


GeomRaster <- proto(Geom, {

draw <- function(., data, scales, coordinates, ..., interpolate=TRUE)
{
with(coordinates$transform(data, scales),
{
ux <- sort(unique(x[!is.na(x)]))
xwid <- mean(diff(ux))

uy <- sort(unique(y[!is.na(y)]))
ywid <- mean(diff(uy))

ncolumns <- length(ux)
nrows <- length(uy)

xlow <- ux[1] - 0.5 * xwid
xhigh <- ux[ncolumns] + 0.5 * xwid

ylow <- uy[1] - 0.5 * ywid
yhigh <- uy[nrows] + 0.5 * ywid

## create a suitable matrix of colors
zmat <- rep("transparent", ncolumns * nrows)
idx <- match(x, ux)
idy <- match(y, rev(uy)) # image goes top to bottom
id <- idy + nrows * (idx-1L)

zmat[id] <- fill

dim(zmat) <- c(nrows, ncolumns)
grid.raster(as.raster(zmat), interpolate = interpolate,
x = xlow, y = ylow,
width = xhigh - xlow, height = yhigh - ylow,
just = c("left", "bottom"),
default.units = "native")

ggname(.$my_name(), rasterGrob(as.raster(zmat),
interpolate = interpolate,
x = xlow, y = ylow,
width = xhigh - xlow, height
= yhigh - ylow,
just = c("left", "bottom"),
default.units = "native", gp=gpar())
)})
}

objname <- "raster"

default_stat <- function(.) StatIdentity
default_aes <- function(.) aes(colour=NA, linetype=1, alpha = 1)
required_aes <- c("x", "y", "fill")
guide_geom <- function(.) "polygon"

examples <- function(.) {
ggplot(melt(volcano), aes(x=X1, y=X2, fill=value)) + geom_raster()
}
}
)

geom_raster <- GeomRaster$build_accessor()


p <-
ggplot(melt(volcano), aes(x=X1, y=X2, fill=value)) +
geom_raster() +
scale_x_continuous(expand=c(0,0))+
scale_y_continuous(expand=c(0,0))

p + coord_cartesian(xlim=c(20, 50), ylim=c(30,70))


For some reason this code fails when setting xlim or ylim.

Anyway, that may be a start. Should anyone wish to improve it, please
let me know.

baptiste

Thanks! :)
Really cool to see that you've done it! and to be able to plot this…

Actually, I realize that what you wrote provides much more flexibility
that what I'm looking for especially the ability to choose the colour
scale… but this comes at the price of being much slower than the
background method. Example follows with a "real life" 1392 x 1040
picture:

plbg <- qplot(0, 0) +
opts(panel.background = backgroundFullPlot(myImg)) +
coord_cartesian(xlim = c(0, xmax-1), ylim=c(ymax-1, 0))

system.time({
ggsave("comparison-bg.pdf", plbg)
})
#Saving 9" x 8" image
#utilisateur système écoulé
# 3.313 0.993 4.426


plraster <- qplot(0, 0) +
geom_raster(aes(x=X2, y=X1, fill=value), data=melt(myImg@grey),
colour=1, group=1, size=1) +
coord_cartesian(xlim = c(0, xmax-1), ylim=c(ymax-1, 0))

system.time({
ggsave("comparison-raster.pdf", plraster)
})
#Saving 9" x 8" image
#utilisateur système écoulé
# 82.658 13.441 107.855


Based on your code, I will try to write a geom_background() that would
take only one aesthetics (pixmap?) and plot it on background… Does not
sound like very ggplot2 spirit. Any help or comment welcome.

Best, Thomas

parts:
I don't know why it's so slow, but I suspect it's more to do with a
general ggplot2 behavior rather than this particular geom. Consider
this dummy example,

p = ggplot(melt(matrix(rnorm(1e6),1e3))) + geom_blank(aes(X1,X2))
system.time(print(p))
user system elapsed
21.181 4.636 25.793

It takes over 25s on my machine, with nothing to draw whatsoever. I
guess it's dragging the data around and reshaping it needlessly (?),
perhaps.

With geom_point,

p = ggplot(melt(matrix(rnorm(1e6),1e3))) + geom_point(aes(X1,X2))
system.time(print(p))
user system elapsed
74.993 11.497 89.378

the timing is similar to that of geom_raster,

p = ggplot(melt(matrix(rnorm(1e6),1e3))) + geom_raster(aes(X1,X2,fill=value))
system.time(print(p))
user system elapsed
56.069 9.753 67.440

Geoms add layers to the plot, so I don't think your idea of
geom_background can work.

baptiste

parts:
Right…

Concerning your point about the problem with using a geom, is there a
way to pass the actual xlim and ylim to backgroundFullPlot?
Otherwise, I'll end up setting some xlim and ylim var before the plot
and pass it to coord_cartesian and backgroundFullPlot but it's really
dirty…

backgroundFullPlot = function(picture)
return(function() rasterGrob(picture, x = unit(0.5, "npc"), y =
unit(0.5, "npc"), width = unit(1, "npc"), height = unit(1, "npc")))

ggplot()+opts(panel.background = backgroundFullPlot(firstPhaseImg))

Thomas
